notes: Breadboard hole names follow the image's row letters: the image's upper half is labelled j–f and the lower half e–a. I used bank 'b' for the upper half (rows f–j) and 't' for the lower half (rows a–e), as the catalogue's row letters imply.

Column numbers are read from the picture. The button sits across the centre gap at columns 4 and 6. Only the two lower legs are visible, so the upper legs (4b.f and 6b.f) are assumed. They are in the same columns, across the gap.
Which button ports (1.l, 1.r, 2.l, 2.r) go to which legs is arbitrary, because the button's two sides are symmetric.

Signal path: Arduino pin 2 → teal wire → column 6 upper half. Column 6 is the button leg and, through its lower half, the 10k resistor's first leg. The resistor's other leg is in column 9, which a black wire takes to the GND rail.
The orange wire joins button column 4 to the + (5V) rail. A red wire joins Arduino 5V to the same rail. A black wire joins Arduino GND to the − rail.
Rail hole numbers (bp.1, bp.3, bn.1, bn.7) are estimated from the picture, counting holes from the left end of the bottom rails.
The 10k resistor is stored as value=10000.
The Arduino–USB cable for serial communication is not drawn in the circuit, so it is not included.
